chunks: From him, from Ibn Mahboub, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
Justice is sweeter than honey, softer than butter, and more fragrant than musk.
ai.seo_question: What are the sensory metaphors used to describe justice in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to illustrate that justice (al-'Adl) is an intrinsic virtue that brings sensory and spiritual delight, rather than a burdensome duty. By comparing justice to honey, butter, and musk, the Imam highlights its natural appeal and the comfort it brings to the heart, a concept central to Shia theological emphasis on justice as a divine attribute and human ideal. This sensory imagery serves to motivate individuals to embody fairness in their personal conduct and governance.
